description_en: A unique feature of this Phalcā at Cīthū Ṭola is a 17th-century stone ṭorana functioning as an entrance, guarded by stone lions. This distinctive rest house has a rich history. Several medieval inscriptions refer to the locality as 'Cusathuri,' which later evolved into ‚Cīthū‘. It was one of the six main quarters (ṭola) of Kirtipur in the 17th century (Ś. ŚreṣṭhaVS 2057, p.29).Inside the Phalcā, an enclosed shrine houses the primary Gaṇeśa (sthānagaṇeśa) of Cīthū Ṭola. This Gaṇeśa is worshipped not only by local residents but also by people from neighboring areas such as Lvahaṃdegaḥ, Mānaḥtvāḥ, and Kusicā. It is noteworthy that the original Gaṇeśa statue and a wooden toraṇa were stolen in the 1960s and subsequently replaced with new ones (Shokoohys and Śreṣṭha2014, p.280-281).Adjacent to the main shrine, another stone statue of Gaṇeśa is installed in a wall niche. This Gaṇeśa is depicted seated on a serpent and sheltered by a hood of serpents—an iconography that is rare in the Kathmandu Valley. Animal sacrifices are prohibited at this shrine, earning the deity the namehi matvaṃmha Ganedyaḥ, meaning “the Gaṇeśa who does not consume blood” (according to a local resident, Maharjana, male, age 69).A particularly notable feature is the massive free-standing stone gate positioned in front of Cīthū Phalcā’s western bay, a unique element not found in otherphalcāsin the Valley. The gate’s arch is intricately carved as a toraṇa, featuring a central image of Gaṇeśa,aṣṭamātṛkādeities on either side, and a statue of Bhairava above.Although no inscriptions within Cīthū Phalcā provide direct information about its original construction, the earliest known inscription, dated to 1674 CE (NS 794), records only the year and the name “Custhurī,” an earlier form of the quarter's (Ṭola) name. The stone bearing this inscription closely resembles the stone used for the toraṇa, suggesting that it may document the installation of the toraṇa itself. Shokoohys and Shrestha (2014, p. 282) similarly associate the inscription with the toraṇa. During the recent reconstruction of the phalcā, a stone capital bearing an inscription dated to 1697 CE (NS 817) was discovered, indicating the former presence of a bell mounted on a stone frame.Historically, Cīthū Phalcā was a freestanding structure with a gable roof, as documented in a photograph from the 1970s. This gable roof was later replaced with a shed roof following the construction of a multi-story ward office building adjacent to the phalcā. The 2015 earthquakes caused severe damage, leading to Cīthū Phalcā’s complete reconstruction by the Department of Archaeology in 2021. Additional funding from Kirtipur Municipality supported the installation of carved wooden elements and special bricks used in the cornice.Recent years have seen the introduction of new social practices at the phalcā. In 2021, the Sun Star Club, a local youth organization, initiated a new tradition in which a mound of ritual food (samaybaji) is displayed in front of the phalcā on the full moon day of Bhādra.Another event,hāthu hāyke, was inaugurated on March 1, 2022. This ritual involves a five-foot-tall wooden mask of Bhairava, crafted in Bungamati and permanently installed in Cīthū Phalcā. The inaugural ceremony was marked by the pouring of fermented beer (thvã) from the mouth of the Bhairava mask for participants to drink and receive blessings. The event was formally inaugurated by the Mayor of Kirtipur.As thesthānagaṇeśa, the Gaṇeśa enshrined in the phalcā is visited by local residents before they commence major domestic rituals. The Mānaṃtvāḥ Dāphā Khalaḥ, a group of local dāphā singers, perform devotional songs at the phalcā on the full moon day of Śrāvaṇa. In addition to its ritual functions, the phalcā continues to serve as an important venue for social, political, and cultural gatherings.
description_ne: अन्त कुनैपनि फल्चामा नपाइने १७ औं शदीमा निर्मित ढुङ्गाको तोरण सहितको प्रवेशद्वार भएकाले यो फल्चालाई विशेष तुल्याएको छ ।कीर्तिपुरस्थित चीथू टोलमा यो फल्चा अवस्थित छ । कीर्तिपुरका उत्तरमध्यकालीन थुप्रै अभिलेखहरूमा यस स्थानलाई ‘चुसथुरि’ भनिएको छ । यही शब्द क्रमश जेलिएर ‘चीथू’ हुन आएको स्पष्ट छ । १७ औं शदीताका कीर्तिपुर नगरभित्र ६ वटा मुख्य टोलहरू थिए । ती प्रमुख टोलहरूमध्ये चीथू पनि एक थियो (Ś. ŚreṣṭhaVS 2057, p.29) । मुख्य टोलका रूपमा विकसित यस स्थानमा भएका अनेक स्मारकमध्ये यो फल्चा बेग्लै महत्व र विशेषता बोकेको सम्पदा हो ।यस फल्चामा चीथू टोलका साथै कीर्तिपुरको पूर्वीय खण्डमा पर्ने अन्य टोलहरू ल्वहंदेग:, मान:त्वा:, कुसिचा, बही आदि विभिन्न टोलवासीको स्थानगणेश (Gaṇeśa shrine) पनि रहेको छ । तीन कवलमध्ये गणेशको मूर्तितिर लाग्ने पश्चिमी कवलमा तोरण सहितको ढुङ्गाको प्रवेशद्वार बनाइएको छ । अन्त कतैपनि यस प्रकृतिको शिलाको द्वार फल्चामा पाइँदैन । तोरणको केन्द्रमा गणेशको मूर्ति छ भने दायाँ-बायाँ अष्टमातृका र माथि भैरवको मूर्ति कुँदिएको छ । यस फल्चामा भएको गणेशको पुरानो मूर्ति र त्यसमाथिको काष्ठतोरण सन् १०६० को दशकमा चोरी भएकाले सोही दशक नयाँ प्रति बनाई प्रतिस्थापन गरिएको थियो (ShokoohysandŚreṣṭha2014, p. 280-281) । मूल गणेशका अलावा फल्चामा अर्को एक गणेशमूर्ति छ । नागको शरीरमाथि बसी तिनै नागको फणाले गणेशको शीरलाई ओढाएको दृष्य देखाइएका गणेश उपत्यकामा कमैमात्र पाइन्छन् । भारतमा समेत यस प्रकारको नागफणायुक्त गणेशमूर्ति नपाइँने हुँदा यस शैलीको गणेशमूर्तिले नेपालको मौलिक मूर्तिनिर्माण परम्परालाई झल्काउने तथ्यलाई यहाँ महत्वपूर्ण मान्न सकिन्छ (G.Ṭaṇḍana, VS 2042, 59) । स्थानीयमा यस गणेशलाई बलि चढाउन नहुने मान्यता छ र बोलाचालीमा यसलाईहि मत्वंम्ह गनेद्य:भनिदै आएको छ जसको अर्थ ‘रगत ग्रहण नगर्ने गणेश’ भन्ने हुन्छ (local resident, Mahrarjana, male, age 69) ।फल्चामा अनेक अभिलेख पाइए तापनि  यसको प्रारम्भिक निर्माणसंग सम्बन्धित अभिलेख भने प्राप्त छैन । यहाँ पाइएकामध्ये सबैभन्दा पुरानो अभिलेख नेसं ७९४  (सन् १६७४) को हो । यस अभिलेखमा ‘चुस्थुरी’ भनी टोलको नाम र संवत् मात्र कुँदिएकाले यसले कुन घटना (कार्य) लाई बुझाउन खिजिएको हो भन्ने कुरा ठोकुवा गर्न मुस्किल छ । यो अभिलेख कुँदिएको ढुङ्गा र फल्चामा भएको तोरण कुँदिएको ढुङ्गा समान प्रकृतिका भएकाले सम्भवत: यो अभिलेख फल्चामा तोरण निर्माण पश्चात् राखिएको हो कि भन्ने अनुमान हुन्छ ।ShokoohysandŚreṣṭha(2014, p. 282) ले पनि यस अभिलेखलाई उक्त तोरणसंगै जोडेका छन् फल्चाको पछिल्लो पुन:निर्माणका दौरान  ढुङ्गाको एक मेथ फेला परेको थियो जसमा  नेसं ८१७ (सन् १६९७) को अभिलेख छ । यसबाट कुनै समय यहाँ ढुङ्गाको थामोमा झुण्डिएको घण्टा भएको तथ्य खुल्दछ । यो फल्चा प्रारम्भमा दुईपाखे (hip roof) हुने गर्दथ्यो भन्ने तथ्य सन् १९७० को दशकतिर खिचिएको फोटोबाट खुल्दछ (फोटो हेर्नुहोस्) । सोही दशकतिर फल्चा पछाडि वडा कार्यालयको भवन बनाउने क्रममा फल्चाको छानोलाई एक पाखे बनाइएको थियो । जीर्ण अवस्थामा रहेको पाटी सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पले थप कमजोर बनाए पश्चात् पूरातत्व विभागले सन् २०२१ मा यसको पुन:निर्माणकार्यको थलानी गरेको थियो । बन्दै गरेको पाटीमा कीर्तिपुर नगरपालिकाले पनि थप बजेट निकासा गरी बुट्टेदार थामो र त्यसमाथि मेथ र कार्निस (धलिंम्व: छुँवा, नागबेली, स्वांफ्व:बुट्टा) हाल्ने कार्य गरेको हो । फल्चा पुन:निर्माणकार्य सम्पन्न भई सन् २०२१ सेप्टेम्बर २० तारीखका दिन कीर्तिपुर नगरपालिकाका मेयर रमेश महर्जनले यसको विधिवत् उद्घाटन गरेका हुन्।स्थानीय युवाहरूबाट संचालित सन स्टार क्लब नामक संस्थाले फल्चा पुन:निर्माणको अवसरमासमय्‌बजि पुन्हीका दिन (भाद्र शुक्ल पूर्णिमा) फल्चामा समय्‌बजि र भैरवको मुखाकृति प्रदर्शनमा राखीहाथु हाय्‌केगुसंस्कृतिको शुभारम्भ गर्दै जाने लक्ष राखेको थियो । कीर्तिपुरका विविध मध्यकालीन अभिलेखहरूमा हाथु संस्कृतिको उल्लेखन परेको तर हाल कीर्तिपुरका कुनैपनि फल्चामा सो संस्कृति जीवन्त नरहेको तथ्य महसुस गरी उप्रान्त यस फल्चामा हाथु संस्कृति चलाउँदै जाने लक्ष लिइएको थियो । सो लक्ष अनुरूप सन् २०२१ कोसमय्‌बजि पुन्हीका दिन क्लबले पहिलो पल्ट फल्चामा समय्‌बजि प्रदर्शनमा राखेको थियो । उप्रान्त भैरवको मुखाकृति प्रदर्शनमा राख्ने हेतु सन् २०२१ मार्च १ तारीख (शिवरात्री) का दिन बुङ्गमतीबाट भैरवको ५ फीट अग्लो काष्ठ मुखाकृति फल्चामा स्थापनाका खातिर ल्याइएको थियो । सो मुखाकृति फल्चामा स्थापना गर्ने दिन ठुलो समारोह आयोजन गरी कीर्तिपुर नगरपालिकाका मेयर सहित अन्य अतिथिहरूबाटहाथुसंस्कृतिको पनि शुभारम्भ गरिएको थियो ।कीर्तिपुरको पूर्वी खण्डमा पर्ने विभिन्न टोलवासीको घरमा कुनै प्रकारको संस्कारजन्य पूजा एवं भोज-भटेर हुँदा यस फल्चामा आई गणेश पूज्ने चलन छ । मानंत्वा: दाफा खल:ले प्रतिवर्ष गुंला पुन्हीका दिन फल्चामा उपस्थित भई भजन गायन गर्ने थिति चलाउदै आएको छ । चतुष्कोणाकार ठुलो चोकतिर फर्किएको फल्चा भएकाले चोकतिर दर्शक पर्ने गरी फल्चा अगाडि समय-‍समयमा विविध राजनैतिक, सामाजिक एवं सांस्कृतिक कार्यक्रमहरू हुने गरेका छन् ।

historical_events.event_description: An inscription is embedded into the eastern wall of the Phalcā, which mentions the locality's name as 'Custhurī' and the installation date. However, the exact purpose or significance of the event on that day is unknown. Notably, the color and texture of the stone inscription match those of the stone toraṇa nearby. This suggests that the inscription might have been created around the same time when the toraṇa was constructed. Shokoohys and Śreṣṭha (2014, p. 282) also associate this inscription with the toraṇa, further supporting the idea that they are contemporaneous.

During the reconstruction project in 2019, a significant discovery was made when a worker uncovered a stone fragment of a metha. Upon examination, it was found that the surface of the metha bore an inscription dating back to the Malla period. This metha is believed to be a part of a hanging bell, suggesting that a hanging bell was once present here, suspended from a stone beam. The inscription on the metha records the installation of this bell, shedding light on the historical significance of this site.

During the rule of King Pṛthvī Śāha, a jyāmadāra named Suravīra's sons, namely Kṛṣṇavīra, Kulamāna, and Budhimāna, were responsible for the installation of stone slabs on a specific section of the main lane within the city of Kirtipur. The approximate length of this paving project is described as extending "from the east of Gaḥchẽ Dhvākhā to the west of Chīthū Dhvākhā." This historical record provides insight into the civic development and infrastructure projects undertaken during that period.

historical_events.event_name: Addition of lions and paving of stone
historical_events.event_description: Śemāna, his wife Jīuthakuṃ and other family members facilitated the donation of two lion statues in front of the Gaṇeśa, and also had the front yard paved with stone.
The primary statue of Gaṇeśa (sthāna Gaṇeśa) and the wooden toraṇa above it were stolen during the 1960s to 1970s. Both of these objects were replaced with new ones in the 1980s.
The Phalcā was already in poor condition before the 2015 earthquakes. The tremors further deteriorated its condition. The Department of Archaeology enabled reconstruction in 2021 CE.

Following the completion of the reconstruction project, the Phalcā was officially inaugurated by the Mayor of Kirtipur. As part of this significant event, a mound of samaybaji was exhibited in front of the Phalcā. This exhibition marked a historic occasion, as it was the first time such an event had taken place in the history of the Phalcā.

Various inscriptions from Kirtipur provide historical evidence of the hāthu hayke tradition, where fermented beer (thvã) is discharged from a Bhairava mask's mouth for people to drink. These inscriptions include one from 1694 CE (NS 814) installed at the Khyālidyaḥ Shrine in Kvāḥcva, another from 1698 CE (NS 818) at the Ichẽ Ṭola, another from 1693 CE (NS 813), and a copperplate inscription from 1703 CE (NS 823), all of which mention thehāthu hāyketradition.In more recent times, the Sun Star Club, a youth organization in Kirtipur, aimed to revive this tradition after the reconstruction of the Phalcā and began planning for it in 2019 CE. Krishna Prasad Maharjan and Arjun Prasad Maharjan, the sons of the late Prem Bahadur Maharjan and Ganesh Kumari Maharjan, provided the generous funding of the crafting the Bhairava mask. The responsibility for carving the mask was entrusted to Laxman Maharjan, one of the ost prominent skilled wood craftsmen from Bungamati. However, Laxman Maharjan passed away due to the coronavirus before finalising the mask. His students, namely Rambhakta Maharjan, Amir Shakya, and Jitendra Tuladhar, took over the carving of the Bhairava mask, which stands at over 5 feet tall, and is thus, as of now, the largest Bhairava mask in Kathmandu Valley.On March 1, 2022, the Bhairava mask was transported from the craftsmen's workshop in Bungamati to Kirtipur. The mask's journey was accompanied by a traditional musical ensemble and a celebratory procession, and it was ultimately installed at the Phalcā as part of the hāthu hāyke tradition's revival.Various inscriptions from Kirtipur reveal the existence of thehāthuhayketradition when fermented beer (thvã) is discharged from a Bhairava mask’s mouth for the people to drink: An inscription from 1694 CE (NS 814) installed at the Khyālidyaḥ Shrine in Kvāḥcva, another inscription from 1698 CE (NS 818) at the Ichẽ Ṭola, another one from 1693 CE (NS 813), and a copperplate inscription from 1703 CE (NS 823) are some inscriptions that mention thehāthuhāyketradition. The Sun Star Club, an organization run by local youths, had aimed to restart the tradition after the reconstruction of the Phalcā and began planning in 2019 CE. Krishna Prasad Maharjan and Arjun Prasad Maharjan, sons of the late Prem Bahadur Maharjan and Ganesh Kumari Maharjan, agreed to provide the funds for carving the large Bhairava mask. Senior wood craftsman from Bungamati Laxman Maharjan was given the responsibility to carve the mask. Unfortunately, he passed away due to the coronavirus. Then, his students Rambhakta Maharjan, Amir Shakya, and Jitendra Tuladhar completed the carving of over 5-feet tall Bhairava mask. On March 1, 2022, the Bhairava mask was brought from the craftsmen’s workshop in Bungamati to Kirtipur in the company of the traditional musical ensemble and pageantry to be installed at the Phalcā.Various inscriptions from Kirtipur provide historical evidence of the hāthu hayke tradition, where fermented beer (thvã) is discharged from a Bhairava mask's mouth for people to drink. These inscriptions include one from 1694 CE (NS 814) installed at the Khyālidyaḥ Shrine in Kvāḥcva, another from 1698 CE (NS 818) at the Ichẽ Ṭola, another from 1693 CE (NS 813), and a copperplate inscription from 1703 CE (NS 823), all of which mention thehāthu hāyketradition.In more recent times, the Sun Star Club, a youth organization in Kirtipur, aimed to revive this tradition after the reconstruction of the Phalcā and began planning for it in 2019 CE. Krishna Prasad Maharjan and Arjun Prasad Maharjan, the sons of the late Prem Bahadur Maharjan and Ganesh Kumari Maharjan, generously agreed to cover the expenses of crafting the Bhairava mask.The responsibility for carving the mask was entrusted to a skilled wood craftsman from Bungamati, Laxman Maharjan. Unfortunately, Laxman Maharjan passed away due to the coronavirus. Subsequently, his students, namely Rambhakta Maharjan, Amir Shakya, and Jitendra Tuladhar, took over the carving of the Bhairava mask, which stands at over 5 feet tall.On March 1, 2022, the Bhairava mask was transported from the craftsmen's workshop in Bungamati to Kirtipur. The mask's journey was accompanied by a traditional musical ensemble and a celebratory procession, and it was ultimately installed at the Phalcā as part of the hāthu hāyke tradition's revival.[1]An inscription from 1694 CE (NS 814) installed at the Khyālidyaḥ Shrine in Kvāḥcva, another inscription from 1698 CE (NS 818) at the Ichẽ Ṭola, another one from 1693 CE (NS 813), and a copperplate inscription from 1703 CE (NS 823) are some inscriptions that talk about thehāthuhāyketradition.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of the Bhairava mask inside the phalcā
historical_events.event_description: Consecration rituals were performed on the Bhairava mask for two days when it was enshrined inside the Phalcā.

In keeping with the Newar tradition of visiting other major shrines in the city following the installation of a new statue, a grand procession of devotees was organized to pay homage to other significant Bhairava shrines in the Kathmandu Valley. This procession saw the participation of approximately 1,000 devotees. The procession visited a total of 9 major Bhairava shrines, including Pacalī Bhairava, Kāla Bhairava, Ākāśa Bhairava, Ānanda Bhairava, Vaṭuka Bhairava, Tyāṅgā Bhairava, Hayagrīva Bhairava, along with Kirtipur's own Bāgha Bhairava, Aṣṭasiddhi Bhairava, and the newly installed Bhairava mask at the Phalcā. This pilgrimage allowed devotees to offer their reverence and prayers at these sacred sites.
